rows.value: Zero wages is not zero qualifying income
rows.detail: The income alternative uses MAGI-based monthly household income, not just wages. California’s outreach letter says income from any source, and the enacted state statute (AB 2161) uses MAGI-based financial methods. Zero earned income alone is not an automatic disqualification.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "States must use an individual's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based monthly household income for Medicaid to determine compliance with the community engagement requirement." DHCS member letter (Aug 31, 2026): "Have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours."

rows.detail: If verified monthly MAGI-based household income reaches the federal threshold ($580 at the current $7.25 wage), this is an alternative to tracking 80 activity hours. Financial eligibility for Medi-Cal is a separate test. No personal eligibility determination is made here.
rows.evidence: CMS deck box E: "Have a monthly income that is not less than the applicable Federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours (i.e., $7.25 (in 2026) x 80 = $580 per month)." CMS fact sheet: "or meet it by earning at least 80 times the Federal hourly minimum wage ($580 per month in 2026)". AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours."

rows.item: If qualifying income is below the threshold
rows.detail: Community service, a qualifying work program, at least half-time education, combinations of qualifying hours, or a qualifying exclusion/exception can satisfy or remove the requirement.
rows.evidence: 42 CFR 435.552(a): community engagement is shown by 80 hours of work, community service or a work program, half-time enrollment in an educational program, a combination totaling 80 hours, or the monthly-income test. CMS fact sheet: "Some adults are exempt and do not need to meet the work requirement".

rows.item: If income is too high for Medi-Cal
rows.detail: Apply through the state marketplace for an eligibility decision and plan options. Marketplace savings use expected annual household income; the Medicaid work rule is not a universal requirement to buy insurance.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov: "Marketplace savings are based on your expected household income for the year you want coverage, not last year's income." DHCS Apply page: Covered California — "Apply for Medi-Cal" and "If you don’t qualify, shop for low-cost health plans".

rows.item: Do not intentionally fail the rule
rows.detail: DHCS warns that losing Medi-Cal for not meeting these rules prevents financial help for a Covered California plan. Full-price coverage may be necessary; do not assume subsidized coverage is the fallback.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance."

rows.detail: Federal general deadline is January 1, 2027. The DHCS public work page says January 1, 2027; the MEDIL body says effective January 1, 2027; its enclosed member letter says March 2027. The enacted state statute says "no sooner than January 1, 2027" and only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready. Plan conservatively for January and rely on your county’s individual notices, not an assumed grace period.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "States must generally implement this requirement no later than January 1, 2027." DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Starting January 1, 2027, some adults will need to work, volunteer, go to school, or be in training". MEDIL I 26-25 body: "Section 71119 requires that effective January 1, 2027, MAGI New Adult Group members must also comply with WCER". DHCS member letter: "these rules will not go into effect until March 2027." AB 2161 §14005.69(d): "No sooner than January 1, 2027, ... and following the department's confirmation that systems are programmed to maintain coverage with minimal data requests to an applicable individual, an applicable individual shall demonstrate work or community engagement." AB 2161 §14005.69(q)(1): "This section shall be implemented only after the director determines, and communicates in writing to the Department of Finance, that systems have been programmed for implementation of this section."

rows.detail: Investment interest is counted; MAGI also adds tax-exempt interest. A bank balance and the interest it produces are not the same thing.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov: "Include expected interest and dividends earned on investments, including tax-exempt interest." HealthCare.gov: "MAGI is adjusted gross income (AGI) plus these, if any: untaxed foreign income, non-taxable Social Security benefits, and tax-exempt interest."

rows.detail: HealthCare.gov instructs use of net rental and royalty income, not gross rent receipts. The work-income alternative uses MAGI methodology (42 CFR 435.552(f)(2)). Do not treat every rent deposit as countable profit.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov: "Rental and royalty income — Use net rental and royalty income." 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2): "The agency must determine the monthly income based on the individual's MAGI-based income, for their MAGI-based household, as defined at § 435.603".

rows.detail: Capital gains are listed as income. This does not establish that each particular Kalshi contract is a capital asset or a section 1256 contract.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov lists "Capital gains" among income types to count. IRS Publication 550 discusses traders in securities or commodities generally; it does not classify Kalshi event contracts.

rows.detail: No Kalshi-specific IRS classification was verified. A targeted irs.gov search on 2026-10-19 found no event-contract or Kalshi guidance. Do not assume all contracts are futures eligible for section 1256 or a 60/40 split. General IRS trader guidance is context only, not confirmation for your contracts.
rows.evidence: No official classification located; value intentionally blank.

rows.detail: IRS Publication 550 describes securities/commodities trader gains as generally not subject to self-employment tax, with a dealer exception. This general tax rule does not decide Medicaid activity-hour eligibility or your Kalshi treatment.
rows.evidence: IRS Pub. 550 (2025): "Gains and losses from selling securities or commodities as a trader are not subject to self-employment tax. This is true whether the election is made or not. For an exception that applies to section 1256 contracts, see Self-Employment Income" — which says gains of "a commodity or option dealer's trading in section 1256 contracts" are included in net earnings from self-employment.

rows.detail: Self-employment income is reported after business expenses. Separately paid property-management services and net rental income are different categories; no fee income is assumed for you.
rows.evidence: HealthCare.gov: "Self-employment income — Include the income you expect to make from your business after expenses."

rows.detail: CMS specifies monthly MAGI-based household income for the work-income route. Marketplace premium assistance instead estimates the coverage year’s annual household income. Do not use annual trading turnover as monthly income.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "States must use an individual's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based monthly household income for Medicaid to determine compliance with the community engagement requirement." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours." HealthCare.gov: "Marketplace savings are based on your expected household income for the year you want coverage, not last year's income."

rows.detail: No dollar amounts, tax household, deductions, or contract records were supplied. Personal MAGI and eligibility cannot be confirmed. Unknown is not recorded as $0.
rows.evidence: No personal amounts were supplied; value intentionally blank.

rows.value: $580 per month at current federal wage
rows.detail: Threshold is federal minimum wage × 80, not California minimum wage. CMS requires MAGI-based household income. Income must also stay within applicable Medi-Cal financial eligibility rules.
rows.evidence: CMS deck box E: "Have a monthly income that is not less than the applicable Federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours (i.e., $7.25 (in 2026) x 80 = $580 per month)." CMS deck: "States may not use State or local minimum wages for this calculation." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours."

rows.detail: The six-month average applies only to a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B): "a worker who performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor". Both the enacted California statute and the federal regulation say so. Volatile trading or rental income does not by itself establish seasonal-worker status. The DHCS member letter’s broader wording is flagged at R55.
rows.evidence: CMS deck box F: "Is a seasonal worker and has an average monthly income over the preceding 6 months"; footnote: "A seasonal worker is described in section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7): average monthly income "over the preceding six months" counts only if the individual "is a seasonal worker, as described in Section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the federal Internal Revenue Code of 1986." 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1): seasonal-worker averaging applies "if the individual is a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B)". 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B): "The term ‘seasonal worker’ means a worker who performs labor or services on a seasonal basis as defined by the Secretary of Labor, including workers covered by section 500.20(s)(1) of title 29, Code of Federal Regulations and retail workers employed exclusively during holiday seasons."

rows.detail: CMS includes paid, in-kind and unpaid work; federal rule discussion includes self-employment. Taxable earnings are not the only activity route. Whether your specific work qualifies remains unresolved.
rows.evidence: 42 CFR 435.552(b): "Work means: (i) Work in exchange for money; (ii) Work in exchange for goods or services (“in-kind” work); and (iii) Unpaid work (other than community service ...)." 91 FR 33348 preamble: "Many individuals work for themselves by being self-employed due to starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor, and these activities meet the definition of work at § 435.552(b)."

rows.detail: CMS describes structured unpaid work benefiting the community under an established organization’s oversight, not partisan activity. It can be voluntary or court-mandated.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "Community Service: Means unpaid work (voluntary or court-mandated) with a structured program that is completed for the direct benefit of the community under the auspices of an established organization ... The activity must not serve a partisan purpose." 42 CFR 435.552(b) adds that the organization must track "dates and hours" and give "a point of contact who can confirm the hours completed."

rows.detail: A qualifying program is defined by federal law; CMS includes certain state employment/training and veterans’ programs. Do not assume independent job searching qualifies.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "Work Program: Means a program as defined at section 6(o)(1) of the Food and Nutrition Act (2008)." 42 CFR 435.552(b) lists WIOA title I, Trade Act section 236, state employment and training programs "other than a supervised job search program or job search training program", and DOL/VA veterans programs.

rows.detail: School/institution determines enrollment status. CMS includes qualifying higher education, career/technical, high school and equivalency programs. A generic online course is not automatically sufficient. The DHCS member letter’s “part time” wording is flagged at R60.
rows.evidence: CMS deck: "States must use the school or institution’s determination of student status (full-time, half-time, or less than halftime)." 42 CFR 435.552(b) lists higher education, career and technical education, high school, and state-approved high school equivalency programs.

rows.detail: Combine qualifying work, community service, work-program hours and less-than-half-time educational hours under CMS rules. Half-time education independently satisfies the route.
rows.evidence: 42 CFR 435.552(a)(5): any combination totaling 80 hours, "however, States are not permitted to combine educational program hours with another activity if the individual is enrolled in an educational program at least half-time." CMS deck: credit hours x 3 x 4.33 for less-than-half-time students.

rows.value: Can count as work under the federal definition
rows.detail: The federal rule defines work to include paid, in-kind and unpaid work, and its preamble names property managers paid in free or reduced rent and self-employed business owners as examples. This states the general rule only; whether your own hours are accepted is not confirmed (see R53).
rows.evidence: 91 FR 33348 preamble: "For example, an individual who performs duties as a property manager or building superintendent may receive compensation in the form of free or reduced rent. Under our definition of work at § 435.552(b), the hours the individual spends performing these duties would count toward meeting the 80-hour requirement." 91 FR 33348 preamble: "Many individuals work for themselves by being self-employed due to starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor, and these activities meet the definition of work at § 435.552(b)." 42 CFR 435.552(b): "Work means: (i) Work in exchange for money; (ii) Work in exchange for goods or services (“in-kind” work); and (iii) Unpaid work (other than community service ...)."

rows.detail: No official California or CMS Kalshi-specific approval of personal trading hours was verified. The federal rule counts self-employment and "owning a business" as work, but no official source reviewed addresses own-account event-contract trading. Do not rely on “full-time trader” alone; the income route may be more directly supported if the threshold is met.
rows.evidence: No official determination located; value intentionally blank. Context: 91 FR 33348 preamble: "Many individuals work for themselves by being self-employed due to starting a business, owning a business, or as an independent contractor, and these activities meet the definition of work at § 435.552(b)."

rows.detail: Section 71119 creates community engagement requirements; section 71107 establishes six-month redeterminations for the adult expansion group. This is not merely a proposal.
rows.evidence: Public Law 119-21, July 4, 2025 [H.R. 1], 139 Stat. 72; table of contents: "Sec. 71107. Eligibility redeterminations." and "Sec. 71119. Requirement for States to establish Medicaid community engagement requirements for certain individuals." MEDIL I 26-25: "On July 4, 2025, Sections 71107 and 71119 of H.R.1 (Public Law 119-21), established two new rules".

rows.detail: Issued June 1, published June 3, 2026; legal effective date July 31, 2026. General state implementation deadline January 1, 2027. Federal Register notes a June 29 correction.
rows.evidence: GovInfo 91 FR 33348: "States are required to implement the new requirement no later than January 1, 2027." DATES: "These regulations are effective on July 31, 2026." Federal Register API: correction 91 FR 39028 published 2026-06-29. CMS fact sheet dated June 1, 2026.

rows.detail: Applies to the Medicaid adult group and certain section 1115 populations, subject to exclusions and exceptions. It is not a work mandate for everyone seeking healthcare. Your age and eligibility group are unknown.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: applies to "non-pregnant adults between the ages of 19 and 64 who are not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare and are eligible for or enrolled in the Medicaid adult group or in certain section 1115 demonstrations".

rows.detail: CMS: certain applicants must demonstrate compliance for at least one month before application; current enrollees for one or more months between renewals. California’s enacted statute sets the months: for applicants, the one month immediately before the month of application; for enrollees, any one month between the last determination and the next scheduled redetermination. DHCS outreach says any month since last renewal. Do not infer every month must be documented.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Certain new Medicaid applicants will need to meet the requirement for at least one month before the month in which the applicant applies, and existing Medicaid beneficiaries will need to meet the requirement for one or more months between renewals." AB 2161 §14005.69(d)(1): "for one month immediately preceding the month during which the individual applies"; (d)(2): "for any one month during the period between the individual’s most recent determination or redetermination ... and their next regularly scheduled redetermination". DHCS member letter (Aug 31, 2026): "Have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal."

rows.detail: If the state cannot verify compliance, it must notify the person and allow 30 calendar days to show compliance or exemption. In California the 30 days start on the date the notice is received (deemed 5 days after the date on the notice), coverage continues during that period, and the county must check every other basis of eligibility and offer a fair hearing before denying. Reapplication is allowed at any time.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: the state "must send a notice of noncompliance and provide the individual with 30 calendar days to demonstrate compliance or that the requirement does not apply to them ... Individuals who are disenrolled may reapply at any time". AB 2161 §14005.69(k)(1)(B): "a period of 30 calendar days, beginning on the date on which the notice of noncompliance is received by the individual"; (k)(2): "deemed to have received the notice of noncompliance five days after the date on the notice"; (k)(1)(E): before denying, "Determine whether there is any other basis for eligibility" and "grant the individual an opportunity for a fair hearing."

rows.detail: DHCS outreach promises a written notice explaining what is needed before coverage ends and how to appeal a disputed decision. Open and respond to county notices promptly.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "you will get a notice in writing telling you what you need to do before your Medi-Cal will end. The notice will also tell you what to do if you do not agree with the decision, including your right to appeal." AB 2161 §14005.69(m)(8): the notice must include "The applicable individual’s right to request a state hearing".

rows.detail: For some ACA expansion adults, with listed exceptions. DHCS’s public page says six-month checks start March 1, 2027; the member letter says "Beginning January 2027" and the MEDIL body says section 71107 is effective January 1, 2027. A work-rule exclusion does not automatically prove exemption from all renewal obligations.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Starting March 1, 2027, some Medi-Cal members will have their eligibility checked twice a year instead of once." DHCS member letter: "Beginning January 2027, this rule says that adults, ages 19-64, will get their Medi-Cal eligibility renewed every 6 months". MEDIL I 26-25: "Section 71107 requires that effective January 1, 2027, states must conduct eligibility redeterminations ... once every six months".

rows.value: Children / older adults / other eligibility groups
rows.detail: DHCS lists children 0–18 and adults 65+ outside work rules. CMS includes mandatory exceptions for other qualifying categorically needy groups and Medicare circumstances. This is not a personal finding.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes ("do not apply to"): "Children (0–18)", "Adults 65 and older", "People on Medicare Part A or Part B". CMS deck mandatory exceptions: "Under the age of 19"; "Entitled to or enrolled in Medicare Part A or enrolled in Medicare Part B"; "Described in another mandatory categorically needy eligibility group".

rows.detail: DHCS includes pregnancy and one year after; CMS includes entitlement to postpartum medical assistance.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Pregnant people (during pregnancy and one year after)". CMS fact sheet exemptions: "Pregnant or eligible for postpartum coverage in their state."

rows.value: Dependent child 13 or younger / disabled person
rows.detail: CMS lists parents, guardians, caretaker relatives or family caregivers of a dependent child 13 or younger or a disabled individual, under defined conditions. California’s statute also lists caregivers of "an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation." Being a property manager is not itself a caregiving exclusion.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Parents, guardians, caretaker relatives, or family caregivers of a dependent child 13 years of age and under, or a disabled individual". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(E) (dependent child "13 years of age or younger or a disabled individual") and (b)(2)(F): "The parent, guardian, caretaker relative, or family caregiver of an individual with a chronic or other health condition, disability, or functional limitation."

rows.detail: CMS includes medically frail people or special medical needs significantly impairing compliance; DHCS lists disability and serious physical/mental conditions or substance-use problems. Do not assume every diagnosis automatically qualifies.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Medically frail or otherwise have special medical needs that significantly impair their ability to comply with the requirement". CMS deck: medical frailty "only includes individuals whose physical, mental, or other behavioral health condition significantly impairs the individual’s ability to comply". DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "People with disabilities"; "People with serious physical or mental health conditions, or substance use problems".

rows.detail: CMS specifies a total disability rating; being a veteran alone is not the listed exclusion.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Veterans with a total disability rating". CMS deck: "total (100 percent) disability rating as defined under 38 U.S.C. §1155". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(G): "A veteran with a disability rated as total under Section 1155 of Title 38".

rows.detail: CMS lists American Indians/Alaska Natives and qualifying former foster youth. DHCS describes people under 26 who were in foster care on their 18th birthday; California’s statute lists "Foster youth or former foster youth under 26 years of age" and Indians, Urban Indians, California Indians and people eligible for the Indian Health Service.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet exemptions: "Former foster care youth"; "American Indians and Alaska Natives". DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "People under age 26 who were in foster care on their 18th birthday". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(B)-(D) and (N): "Foster youth or former foster youth under 26 years of age."

rows.detail: CMS lists people meeting TANF work rules, household SNAP recipients subject to SNAP work rules, and participants in qualifying drug/alcohol treatment programs. California calls TANF CalWORKs and SNAP CalFresh; not every recipient is automatically covered.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: "Meet the TANF work requirements or are a member of a household receiving SNAP benefits and are not exempt from the SNAP work requirements"; "Participants in a drug or alcohol rehabilitation or treatment program". DHCS member letter: "Are meeting the CalWORKs work requirement"; "Are receiving CalFresh and are not excused from the CalFresh work program." AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(I)-(K).

rows.detail: CMS lists inmates; DHCS lists release within the last 90 days. These do not establish general Medicaid payment for services while incarcerated.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet exemptions: "Inmates of a public institution". DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "People released from jail or prison in the last 90 days". AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2)(L): "An inmate or former inmate of a public institution released at any point during the three-month period ending on the first day of that month."

rows.detail: CMS allows specified inpatient/medical care, medical travel, disaster and high-unemployment exceptions. DHCS outreach lists these circumstances and promises additional county notices when applicable. No county-level exception is assumed here.
rows.evidence: CMS fact sheet: hardship options for inpatient or certain other medical services, travel for medical care, "a county with an unemployment rate at or above 8% or 1.5 times the national average", and declared emergencies or disasters. DHCS member letter: "If either one of these applies to your county, we will send you another notice." AB 2161 §14005.69(h)(1)-(4); (h)(3) is "subject to a request from the department to the United States Secretary".

rows.detail: DHCS offers Medi-Cal applications through BenefitsCal, Covered California, mail, phone and in person. Its online estimator is not an eligibility decision. No enrollment or application is submitted by this site.
rows.evidence: DHCS Apply: "Four Ways to Sign Up" — Online (BenefitsCal or Covered California), Mail, Phone, In Person. DHCS Qualify: "This is only an estimate. It is not an application for Medi-Cal."

rows.detail: DHCS chart lists $22,025 annual income for a one-person household; 2026 monthly chart lists $1,836 at 138% FPL. These are reference figures, not a determination; your household size is unknown. Covered California’s 2027 chart says Medi-Cal uses the current year’s FPL, so do not carry these amounts forward as verified 2027 limits.
rows.evidence: DHCS Eligibility by FPL: family size 1 = "$22,025" (138% FPL). DHCS Enclosure 1: family size 1, 138% = 1836. Covered California 2027 chart: "Medi-Cal uses FPL limits for the current year, as calculated by the Department of Health Care Services".

rows.detail: Covered California announced $300 million for state subsidies, compared with $190 million, and 2027 assistance up to 200% FPL ($31,920 individual). This is not a blanket replacement for Medi-Cal lost over work-rule noncompliance.
rows.evidence: Covered California, July 21, 2026: "appropriating $300 million in Health Care Affordability Reserve Fund (HCARF), up from $190 million. As a result, Californians with incomes up to 200 percent of the federal poverty level in 2027 ($31,920 for an individual or $66,000 for a family of four) will be eligible for financial help". DHCS member letter: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance."

rows.detail: Covered California’s 2026 guide says the state subsidy requires eligibility for federal advance premium tax credits and the subsidized application. Do not assume state help bypasses the noncompliance restriction.
rows.evidence: Covered California Financial Help Basics: "To receive the California Premium Subsidy, individuals must be eligible for the federal Advanced Premium Tax Credit (APTC) and apply on Covered California’s subsidized application." DHCS member letter: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance."

rows.detail: No general exemption based solely on zero earned income was identified. California’s statute lists the excluded individuals (§14005.69(b)(2)(A)-(N)), deemed-compliance categories ((f)(1)-(5)) and short-term hardships ((h)(1)-(4)); none is based on having no earned income. (f)(5) also covers "any other federally required or approved exemptions outlined in the state plan or waivers"; no zero-earned-income exemption of that kind was found. Use a documented income or activity route, or a qualifying exclusion.
rows.evidence: AB 2161 §14005.69(b)(2), (f), (h) read in full on 2026-10-19. Value left blank because the state plan and waivers referenced in (f)(5) were not reviewed.

rows.value: No property limit for MAGI Medi-Cal; non-MAGI limits apply
rows.detail: DHCS lists "No property limits" for MAGI Medi-Cal (the adult group). Non-MAGI programs require proof of property such as bank accounts or rental homes and have limits: DHCS says the limit is $130,000 for one person through June 30, 2027 and $21,000 from July 1, 2027, for people 65+, people with disabilities, nursing-home residents and families over the federal-tax-rule income limit. Owning rentals does not alone decide MAGI eligibility; the income they produce does.
rows.evidence: DHCS Help Center, Comparison of Medi-Cal Program Rules — MAGI: "No property limits"; Non-MAGI: "Must report and give proof of property such as vehicles, bank accounts, or rental homes" and "Limits to the amount of property in the household". DHCS Medi-Cal Changes (Asset Limits): "Through June 30, 2027: The most you can own (asset limit) is $130,000 for one person"; "Starting July 1, 2027, the asset limit is: $21,000 for one person".

rows.value: Outreach, data-first verification and statutory protections
rows.detail: DHCS says lawmakers invested in resources and promises information on paid or volunteer work, training and schools. The enacted statute requires DHCS to verify compliance through data interfaces (wage data, aid codes, claims and social-services data) and consent-based platforms. Counties must confirm conflicting data with you before any adverse action and consider every other basis of eligibility before denial. None of this is a waiver of the rule.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "California lawmakers have invested in new resources to help you with these new rules." and "We may be able to use information that we already have about you". AB 2161 §14005.69(c)(1)-(2); (i): "When there is a conflict in reliable data sources that adversely impacts the eligibility ... the county shall request the applicant or beneficiary to confirm information before taking any adverse action"; (n): "the department shall consider all other bases of eligibility".

rows.detail: Recommended sequence: use the official application route to establish household, age/category and income eligibility. Do not report $0 total income solely because wages are zero. Applications require your authorization and accurate records.
rows.evidence: DHCS Apply: Four Ways to Sign Up. HealthCare.gov lists rental, investment, capital-gain and self-employment income among income types to count.

rows.value: Suggested records, not a verified checklist
rows.detail: Keep interest statements, net rental calculations, relevant tax records and trading reports organized by month. For self-employment, DHCS’s general application list asks for Schedule C and a profit-and-loss statement for the last three months, and allows self-attestation when there is no proof of income. Exact county documentation for the work rule is not confirmed.
rows.evidence: DHCS Help Center, "Work for myself": "A copy of Schedule C of the most recent tax return"; "A profit and loss statement for the last three months". Self-Attestation: "You may self-attest if you: Do not have proof of income; Receive cash income". HealthCare.gov: "Rental and royalty income — Use net rental and royalty income."

rows.detail: Recommended decision sequence: assess counted income; review exclusions; if needed use a qualifying activity with reliable attendance/hour records. Specific acceptance of Kalshi or property-management logs remains unverified.
rows.evidence: Recommendation built from CMS routes (deck) and DHCS outreach; no official source confirms acceptance of Kalshi or property-management logs for this person.

rows.value: Read notices / renew / appeal if needed
rows.detail: DHCS recommends up-to-date contact details and BenefitsCal for documents, renewals and messages. Respond within deadlines and use the appeal instructions if a decision seems wrong.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "Make sure your county Medi-Cal office has your current contact information"; "BenefitsCal is the official website where you can keep track of your benefits and documents, complete forms, report changes, upload documents, read notifications, and more."

rows.detail: DHCS directs people who do not qualify to Covered California to shop for health plans. Annual MAGI and other eligibility rules determine savings; work-rule denial may preclude financial help. No premium quote can be verified without personal details.
rows.evidence: DHCS Apply (Covered California): "If you don’t qualify, shop for low-cost health plans". HealthCare.gov: "Marketplace savings are based on your expected household income for the year you want coverage, not last year's income." DHCS member letter: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance."

rows.detail: DHCS’s public changes page says "Work at a job and earn at least $580 a month". The September enclosure says income from any source; CMS specifies monthly MAGI-based household income; the enacted statute (AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6)) uses MAGI-based financial methods for the individual’s MAGI-based household budget. This dashboard follows the statute and the CMS standard, but does not guarantee county acceptance of any specific financial record.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Work at a job and earn at least $580 a month". DHCS member letter (Aug 31, 2026): "Have an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month since your last renewal." CMS deck: "States must use an individual's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based monthly household income for Medicaid to determine compliance with the community engagement requirement." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours."

rows.item: Your own property-management hours and records
rows.detail: Not confirmed for you: whether your county accepts hours spent managing your own rentals, and what records it wants. The corrected federal rule says a state may not deny eligibility "solely because the individual is unable to produce documentation where none exists". Suggested preparation (a recommendation, not a requirement): a dated duty and hours log, leases and rent-credit agreements, and Schedule C/E records.
rows.evidence: 42 CFR 435.557(b)(2)(iii)(B) as corrected at 91 FR 39028: the agency "May not deny or terminate eligibility solely because the individual is unable to produce documentation where none exists or is reasonably available". No county procedure for owner-managed rentals was located.

rows.detail: Amends Welfare and Institutions Code §14005.69. It requires the rule "no sooner than January 1, 2027" and only after DHCS confirms its systems are ready. It sets the look-back months, the MAGI-based income test and seasonal-worker-only averaging. It adds a 30-day cure period running from receipt of the notice and requires the county to check other bases of eligibility before denial. DHCS county guidance ACWDL 25-30 is labelled preliminary and predates it.
rows.evidence: AB 2161: "CHAPTER 209 ... Approved by Governor September 14, 2026. Filed with Secretary of State September 14, 2026." AB 2161 §14005.69(d): "No sooner than January 1, 2027, ... and following the department's confirmation that systems are programmed to maintain coverage with minimal data requests to an applicable individual, an applicable individual shall demonstrate work or community engagement." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(6): "a total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget, that is no less than the applicable minimum wage requirement under Section 206 of Title 29 ... multiplied by 80 hours."

rows.value: Statute: seasonal workers only · member letter: “hours change frequently”
rows.detail: The DHCS member letter (August 31, 2026) says people "whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs" can average $580 over six months. The enacted statute (September 14, 2026), the federal regulation and DHCS’s own Medi-Cal Changes page limit averaging to seasonal workers ("Be a seasonal worker and earn an average of $580 a month"). Do not rely on averaging to cover months when trading or rental income is irregular.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "People whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs can average at least $580 per month from any source over 6 months." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(7): average monthly income "over the preceding six months" counts only if the individual "is a seasonal worker, as described in Section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the federal Internal Revenue Code of 1986." 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1): seasonal-worker averaging applies "if the individual is a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B)". DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Be a seasonal worker and earn an average of $580 a month over the last six months".

rows.value: Data first; documentation required when reasonably available from 2028
rows.detail: The state must check reliable information it already has before asking you. Before January 1, 2028 it may require documentation or accept other information. From January 1, 2028 it must require documentation whenever documentation is reasonably available. It must accept other information when none is available, and may not deny solely for missing documents that do not exist.
rows.evidence: 91 FR 39028 (corrected §435.557): "The agency must establish processes to use reliable information available to the State ... before requesting additional information from the individual"; "(i) Before January 1, 2028, the agency may require documentation or accept other information"; "(ii) Beginning on January 1, 2028 ... the agency must require documentation whenever documentation is reasonably available"; "(iii)(A) Accept information other than documentation ... when there is no reasonably available documentation". AB 2161 §14005.69(j).

rows.value: From January 1, 2027: one month for adults without children
rows.detail: DHCS says that starting January 1, 2027, Medi-Cal will pay one month of medical bills from before you applied for adults without children, and two months for everyone else. This is separate from the work rule. Today’s Help Center still describes the current three-month retroactive period.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Adults without children: Medi-Cal will pay for one month of past medical bills. Everyone else: Medi-Cal will pay for two months of past medical bills." DHCS Help Center: "Retroactive Medi-Cal may help pay medical or dental bills in any of the three months before the application date."

rows.value: Covered California: previous year · Medi-Cal: current year
rows.detail: Covered California’s 2027 chart says marketplace programs use the previous year’s FPL, while Medi-Cal uses the current year’s FPL as calculated by DHCS. It lists the California State Subsidy at 100%–200% FPL and says income above 400% FPL is not eligible for a federal premium tax credit. A 2027 DHCS Medi-Cal chart was not located.
rows.evidence: Covered California 2027 chart: "Covered California uses FPL limits from the previous year to determine eligibility for its programs."; "Medi-Cal uses FPL limits for the current year, as calculated by the Department of Health Care Services"; "*Consumers with income above 400% FPL are not eligible for a federal premium tax credit."; "California State Subsidy | 100%-200% FPL".

rows.detail: DHCS’s Medi-Cal Changes page says copayments from October 1, 2028 apply to adults 19–64 who "Make more than $15,560 a year". DHCS’s own 2026 chart lists the one-person poverty guideline as $15,960. The two figures do not match, so no copayment threshold is stated here. Flagged for review.
rows.evidence: DHCS Medi-Cal Changes (Copayments): "Make more than $15,560 a year". DHCS 2026 FPL Enclosure 1: family size 1, annual FPL 15960.

rows.value: Statute and rule: at least half-time · member letter: “at least part time”
rows.detail: The DHCS member letter says "Go to school at least part time". The enacted statute, the federal regulation and DHCS’s Medi-Cal Changes page all require enrollment at least half-time, with less-than-half-time hours counted only in combination with other activities. Rely on the half-time standard; the school decides your enrollment status.
rows.evidence: DHCS member letter: "Go to school at least part time in any month since your last renewal." AB 2161 §14005.69(e)(4): "The individual is enrolled in an educational program at least half-time." 42 CFR 435.552(a)(4): "enrolled in an educational program at least half-time." DHCS Medi-Cal Changes: "Go to school at least half-time (usually two or three classes, or about six to eight credits each semester)".
